x: George was slowly increasing his lead and Arthur Thomson(Met) had firmly established himself in second place. At four miles, however, Thomson was closing on our lad and nearing the finish he gained the upper hand and went on to win by some 100 yards in 52 mins 15 secs.
In the earlier stages, it did seem that George Williams might well gain second place but he was passed, first by Arthur Thomson and later by Bob Clark.

Arthur Thomson of Metropolitan led from start to finish and beat his team mate Don Thompson by nearly 2 mins. in 76:54. Our first man home was Bob Barnes (9th in 84:01) followed by Cameron (19th in 89 22 and Fotheringham (21st in 93:19).

By the two-mile stage, two County Champions of the previous week came under the Judges' ban, Arthur Thomson (Mddx) and our own Ray Middleton (Surrey), while others who were disqualified included Godbeer, (Cambridge).

Ray Middleton finished a meritorious third behind Williams and Arthur Thomson of Metropolitan. In all fairness, however, we must admit that the redoubtable Matthews was disqualified at 3¾ miles when leading by 52 secs.

The individual race was well and truly won by Paul Nihill (Surrey WC) who had a margin of some 47 secs on the second man home Bob Clark (Poly) with Arthur Thomson (Met.WC) just easing himself into third spot.

The come-back of Met's Arthur Thomson contributed to our defeat and his club is a threat once again. Several other walkers were also making come-backs not least our own George Williams, a former winner.
Junior Martin Bennett managed a fast 14:16.2 for 3000m at Crystal Palace on Wednesday March 21st in the Southern Counties Meeting, only a second behind former international Arthur Thomson.
